- `new` returns `Self::default()`.

behavioral: The tests adequately cover the obligations in `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.OpenAiConfig`. I read all the supplied tests. The `agent_config.settings` and `agent_config.serialization` contracts supply the defaults and serialization rules.

- **Builders and empty start.**
  - `config.rs#mod[tests]/fn[backend_builders_set_only_the_requested_fields]` checks that `OpenAiConfig::new()` serializes to `{}`.
  - It then applies `model`, `endpoint`, `api_key_env`, `api_key` and `option`, and asserts the exact serialized object.
  - A repeated `option("a", ..)` replaces the earlier value and keeps `b`.
- **Serde and the other trait implementations.**
  - `fn[all_backends_preserve_nested_settings_and_credentials]` round-trips an OpenAI config with model, endpoint, `api_key` and nested options, through both `Value` and string forms. It asserts equality, so `PartialEq`, `Serialize` and `Deserialize` are exercised.
  - `fn[openai_inference_options_only_fill_missing_defaults]` compares `AgentConfig::OpenAi(OpenAiConfig::new())` with the config deserialized from `{"backend":"openai"}`.
  - `Default` is covered by `OpenAiConfig::default()` in `fn[option_defaults_and_credential_resolution_are_deterministic]`.
  - `Clone` and `Debug` have no behavior in this requirement's text beyond being derived.
- **Omitted settings use the defaults.**
  - `fn[option_defaults_and_credential_resolution_are_deterministic]` asserts the default model `gpt-6.1-sol` and the default endpoint `https://api.openai.com/v1`.
  - The same test asserts the default options `max_output_tokens` 16384 and `reasoning.effort` low.
  - `fn[openai_inference_options_only_fill_missing_defaults]` asserts that user-supplied options are kept and only missing ones are filled. It covers a user `max_output_tokens`, `reasoning` with only `summary` (so `effort` is filled), and `reasoning` with `effort` set (kept).
  - `fn[openai_uses_the_default_credential_variable]` re-runs the test binary as a child process with `OPENAI_API_KEY` set. It asserts that `resolved_api_key` returns that value, which suits the process-wide environment.
- **Credential overrides.**
  - A missing custom `api_key_env` produces an error naming that variable.
  - An explicit `api_key` wins over the environment.
  - Missing and empty variables are rejected.
- **Overrides take effect end to end.**
  - `configured.rs#mod[tests]/fn[supplied_openai_backend_runs_independent_calls_against_a_local_transport]` runs a supplied OpenAI config against a local transport. It asserts the request model is `local-test`, the default `max_output_tokens` is applied, and the key is not persisted.
- **Public type shape.** `tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]` checks the public export inventory against the book. The `#[non_exhaustive]` attribute and field types are structural.

I found no obligation without a test, and no plausible violation that these assertions would accept.

text: Overrides the SDK’s OpenAI model, endpoint, credentials, or inference options. Omitted settings use the defaults in the agent configuration contract.
pub fn model(self, model: String) -> Self;
pub fn endpoint(self, endpoint: String) -> Self;
pub fn api_key_env(self, api_key_env: String) -> Self;
pub fn api_key(self, api_key: SecretString) -> Self;
pub fn option(self, key: String, value: OptionValue) -> Self;
Each `AgentConfig` variant carries the corresponding settings from
`trust_but_verify::agent`. Serde uses the `backend` field to select `bedrock`,
`openai`, or `ollama` and reads the settings from the same object.
All three backend constructors start with an empty `options` map. Calling
`option(key, value)` inserts one inference setting. Calling it again with the
same key replaces its value and preserves the other settings. An `OptionValue` is
option values and maps associate strings with option values. These serialize as
the corresponding untagged values. Backend calls reject nonfinite floats,
including those nested in an array or map.
`SecretString`, and an optional `session_token` of the same type. Construct a
Serialization preserves the string, while `Debug` prints `<redacted>`.
`AgentConfig` and its backend-specific configuration types implement Serde
serialization and deserialization. An application can embed them in its own
configuration types; serializing and deserializing a supported configuration
An OpenAI configuration MAY omit `model`; the effective model MUST then be
`gpt-6.1-sol`. When `options.reasoning.effort` is omitted, the request MUST use
`low` effort, preserving other reasoning options. When `options.max_output_tokens`
is omitted, the request MUST use an output-token limit of 16,384. These option
defaults MUST apply even when the model is overridden. An explicit model,
reasoning effort, or output-token limit MUST override its corresponding default.
Defaults MUST NOT be written into omitted configuration fields on serialization.
An explicitly empty model MUST still be rejected.
